statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 6 sits well below the block threshold while stress remains in the high band on unresolved energy and trade channels.
recommendation: Conditions are consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour: the cash-open downside leg is fully retraced, volatility has decayed to the session low, and no repeated extension after failed retracements is observed. The narrow flagged window covers the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour and closing auction, where rebalancing flow meets unusually wide sector dispersion.
headline: NQ extends its retracement to 29,628 with VIX back at the day low, while a reported Hormuz arrangement pares Brent from its session high
body: NQ futures trade near 29,628.25, up 0.21% on the session, inside a 29,425.00 to 29,764.75 day range. The cash-open downside leg that briefly lifted tail to 15 three hours ago has not resumed; price has instead extended its recovery, sitting roughly 200 points above the session low, above the 29,544.15 prior close and in the upper half of the range. That is why tail eases to 6. The structure that overwhelms this strategy is repeated extension after failed retracements, and the observed path continues to be its opposite. The cash index agrees, with the Nasdaq-100 at 29,585.81, up 0.14%, inside a 29,400.70 to 29,655.73 range. Volatility has decayed further rather than stabilised: VIX at 15.29 is down 0.07% and now sits at the low end of a 15.22 to 15.94 day range, having fully given back the morning spike. The rates channel is quiet, with the 10-year yield at 4.788%, up less than half a basis point, inside a narrow 4.760 to 4.800 range. Index internals stay sharply split, which keeps the dominant mode at mixed rather than trend-up or trend-down. Semiconductors lead decisively after Qualcomm's multi-generation custom-silicon agreement with Amazon Web Services, which included a warrant for up to 25 million QCOM shares and lifted the stock as much as 9.5%; Intel is up around 5% and Oracle around 5% ahead of Thursday's earnings. Against that, the Dow is down roughly 1.05% at 52,850.92 and the S&P 500 is down 0.38% at 7,688.99. Shared Finviz cross-asset context collected at 16:52 UTC is inside the freshness limit and confirms the split without being treated as live price-path evidence: NQ +0.03% against ES -0.41% and YM -1.13%, with semiconductors 6 of 7 higher on a latest-session basis and megacaps evenly divided 4 to 4. Rotation into a single-name silicon catalyst against broad cyclical weakness is not index-level one-way pressure. The energy channel has eased at the margin. WTI near $92.05 is up 0.62%, but Brent near $96.97 is now down 0.19% after trading as high as $99.46, and reporting that Iran and Oman are close to finalising a temporary safe-transit arrangement for the Strait of Hormuz is the counterweight to the Houthi strikes that halted operations at several Saudi energy facilities. The outage duration remains unresolved, which is why stress stays in the high band at 68 rather than falling further. Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on about $20 billion of U.S. goods took effect today, keeping the North American trade channel live into Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI. The scheduled US 3-year note auction at 17:00 UTC falls inside the current hour; no auction outcome is confirmed at this assessment cutoff, so it is carried as a checkpoint rather than as a result. The flagged window has been moved forward to the 19:00 to 20:00 UTC power hour and closing auction, where Consumer Credit prints and index rebalancing flow concentrates into the widest sector dispersion of the session.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed inside the EA_ON band throughout, with tail between 5 and 10 until the 14:00 UTC slot, where it stepped up to 15 on an observed cash-open downside leg that left NQ near the session low, then fell back to 8 and 7 once that leg was retraced. Stress rose steadily from the low 60s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to a peak of 72 in early Tuesday afternoon as crude extended on the Saudi facility strikes and the North American trade channel reopened, and has since eased slightly. The dominant mode sat at mixed for most of the window because cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action, turning to normal during the quiet overnight hours and to trend-down only for the single hour that carried the decline. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon opens with the cash-open decline retraced and extended, conditional tail at 6 and volatility at the session low. It steps up modestly into the 19:00 UTC power hour and the 20:00 UTC closing auction, where Consumer Credit and index rebalancing flow meet the widest sector dispersion of the session; that pair of hours is the flagged window. Conditional tail then falls to the horizon floor of 5 overnight through the Asian session, with the 07:00 UTC European open on 9 September and the 13:30 UTC US cash open as the next flow checkpoints. The hour after that open carries the horizon peak at 13, because opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure capable of overwhelming mean reversion. Every one of the 24 slots stays inside the EA_ON band. Three unresolved channels could force a step change in either direction: Middle East energy, where the halted Saudi facility operations have no confirmed restart date but a reported Iran-Oman Hormuz arrangement now cuts the other way; the North American trade dispute after Canada's tariffs took effect today; and rate expectations into Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI. Stress stays in the high band throughout because none of those channels is resolved, while confidence decays overnight as the live evidence base ages and recovers once the 9 September cash session provides fresh observable structure.
